title: When AI Skills Outrank the MBA
subtitle: PwC finds 86% of U.S. financial-services executives say AI training beats an MBA for many new hires. A composite CFO at Narmada Capital must fill six analyst seats before campus season closes.
description: HBS-style teaching case dated 8 September 2026. Publicly reported facts: Bloomberg Law (Jo Constantz, 3 Aug 2026) — PwC survey of more than 1,000 U.S. financial-services executives: 86% say AI training is more valuable than an MBA for many new hires; 91% are raising pay for AI skills. Deloitte UK CFO Survey (1–13 July 2026): 96% expect higher technology spend over five years; 93% within 12 months; 78% expect AI to lift productivity in five years; graduate hiring slowed by cost control. JUST Capital (4 Sep 2026): 49% of students and recent grads say school did not prepare them to use AI; 47% of recent grads fear AI will shrink entry-level chances. NACE Job Outlook Nov 2025 update: 13.3% of jobs require AI skills; 10.5% of entry-level postings mention AI. Composite firm: Narmada Capital. Composite decision-maker: CFO Ananya Sen.
thumbnail: 86% SAY AI BEATS THE MBA. WHO DO YOU HIRE?
sources: Jo Constantz, Bloomberg Law, 3 August 2026. AI Skills More Valuable Than MBAs, 86% of Finance Executives Say. PwC survey of 1,000+ U.S. financial-services executives.
Deloitte UK CFO Survey, fieldwork 1–13 July 2026, reported by IBTimes UK, 21 July 2026.
JUST Capital, 4 September 2026. Does Gen Z Feel Ready To Thrive In an AI-Powered Economy?
NACE Job Outlook November 2025 Update, as cited by Higher Ed Insights, 11 June 2026: 13.3% of jobs require AI skills; 10.5% of entry-level jobs mention AI.
Federal Reserve Bank of New York: unemployment among recent college graduates 5.6% in March 2026 (as cited by Higher Ed Insights).
Purdue University Board of Trustees, 12 December 2025: mandatory AI working-competency graduation requirement for undergraduates entering fall 2026.
